title: You don’t wake up one morning and decide,
paragraphs:
You don’t wake up one morning and decide,
“I will walk away from God today.”
No.

It’s quieter than that.
More dangerous than that.
It happens in inches… not miles.
“Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God.” — Hebrews 3:12
Read that again.

Not just sinful behavior.
Not just bad habits.
An unbelieving heart.
That’s where it begins.
At first, nothing looks wrong.

You still show up.
Still smile.
Still know the songs.
Still say “Amen.”
But something underneath is shifting.

Prayer becomes shorter… then optional… then absent.
The Word becomes familiar… then neglected… then avoided.
Conviction becomes uncomfortable… then inconvenient… then ignored.
And nobody notices.
Not yet.
Here’s the truth most people don’t want to say out loud:
You can look spiritually alive on the outside while slowly dying on the inside.
Jesus warned about this kind of life.
“These people honor me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
Far.

Not suddenly gone.
Just… drifting.
But here’s what we miss—

Drifting is not passive.
It is powered by deception.
“…that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.” — Hebrews 3:13
Sin lies.
It whispers gently at first:

“It’s just stress.”
“It’s just a phase.”
“You deserve this.”
“God understands.”
“You can fix this later.”
But every lie has a direction.
Away from God.

And the longer you listen,
the quieter conviction becomes.

The things that once broke you…
no longer move you.

The Word that once cut deep…
now feels dull.

The presence of God that once satisfied you…
now feels distant.
Not because God moved.
But because your heart did.
Let me say something heavy… but necessary:

A hardened heart doesn’t happen overnight.
It happens one compromise at a time.

One secret.
One delay.
One “later.”
One quiet disobedience.

Until one day,
you don’t feel what you used to feel anymore.
And that scares you…

Or worse—
it doesn’t.
But listen carefully.
This is not written to condemn you.
This is written to wake you up.
Because if you can still feel conviction while reading this…
You are not gone.
You are being called back.
“And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you…” — Ezekiel 36:26

God is not intimidated by your drift.
He is not shocked by your struggle.
He is not done with your story.
But He is calling you to respond.
Now.
This is where grace enters the scene.

Not soft grace.
Not permissive grace.
Saving grace. Transforming grace. Redeeming grace.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Not when you were strong.
Not when you were consistent.
Not when you had it all together.
While you were drifting.
Christ died.
And because of that—
You don’t have to stay where you are.

You don’t have to keep pretending.
You don’t have to keep performing.
You don’t have to keep slowly walking away.
You can turn.
Right now.
“Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.” — James 4:8

Not “maybe.”
Not “eventually.”
He will.
So if your heart feels cold…
Come back.
If your fire has faded…
Come back.
If sin has been growing in secret…
Come back.
If you’ve been wearing a mask in church while starving inside…
Come back.
Jesus is not waiting with rejection.
He is waiting with nail-scarred hands.

Ready to forgive.
Ready to restore.
Ready to bring dead places back to life.
“The one who comes to me I will never cast out.” — John 6:37
Never.

Not you.
Not now.
Not ever.
Don’t normalize the drift.

Don’t rename distance as “growth.”
Don’t call numbness “peace.”
Don’t delay obedience again.
Because slow drift leads to real distance.
And real distance leads to dangerous places.
But here is the hope that changes everything:
Jesus specializes in bringing wanderers home.
Every time.
Fully.
Completely.
So today—choose differently.

Choose repentance over delay.
Choose truth over comfort.
Choose Christ over compromise.
And watch what happens to your heart.
This might be your moment.

Your warning.
Your invitation.
Your turning point.
